jobDescription: We design and manufacture washing machines and tumble dryers sold under three consumer brands. The Embedded Software Engineer develops motor-control and user-interface firmware for the next generation of washer control boards, implements the IEC 60730 Class B self-tests, maintains the unit-test and hardware-in-the-loop suites and supports the factory end-of-line test team when new firmware reaches the production testers. Safety-related firmware changes may only be signed off by engineers who hold a functional safety engineer qualification that covers software, so this is a firm requirement for the role.
requirements: Develops embedded C firmware for motor control or user interfaces on 32-bit microcontrollers.
Implements IEC 60730 Class B self-test routines.
Holds a functional safety engineer qualification covering software, for example the TÜV Rheinland Functional Safety Engineer.
Maintains unit-test and hardware-in-the-loop test suites.
Supports the factory end-of-line test team with firmware releases.

evidence.text: Firmware Engineer, Kellingate Home Appliances (September 2021 to July 2026): wrote the BLDC motor-control loop for a dishwasher circulation pump in C on an STM32 microcontroller and tuned it on the bench with the hardware team.
Implemented the Class B RAM, ROM-CRC and clock self-tests required under IEC 60730 for the dishwasher main board and documented them for the external test laboratory.
Functional Safety Engineer (Software), TÜV Rheinland programme, certificate ID FS/SW 18820/24, awarded March 2024.

Maintained the Unity unit-test suite and the hardware-in-the-loop rig that replays door, water-level and temperature signals into the main board overnight, and released the tested builds to the factory programming station.
Graduate Engineer, Osprey Meters (September 2019 to August 2021): wrote drivers for the LCD and pulse inputs of a domestic gas meter.

Work sample: an excerpt from the Class B self-test design note for the dishwasher main board, listing each self-test, its trigger interval, the fault reaction and the laboratory test case it maps to, with the test laboratory's review comments.
Recruiter verification: certificate ID FS/SW 18820/24 was checked on TÜV Rheinland's public database of certified functional safety engineers and is listed under the candidate's name.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate has asked to see the end-of-line test area during the second interview and is available to start from 1 December.

propositions.text: The candidate holds the TÜV Rheinland Functional Safety Engineer (Software) certificate, awarded in March 2024 and listed on TÜV Rheinland's public database.
propositions.rationale: The resume lists the certificate ID and the recruiter verification records the database check.

propositions.text: The candidate implemented IEC 60730 Class B RAM, ROM-CRC and clock self-tests for a dishwasher main board.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the self-tests and the work sample shows the design note with the laboratory's comments.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote a BLDC motor-control loop in C on an STM32 microcontroller.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the motor-control work directly.

gold.expectedGap: Direct support of a factory end-of-line test team is not documented; the sources show tested builds released to the factory programming station.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the verified functional safety certificate and the documented Class B, motor-control and test-suite work; do not extend the build hand-over into support of end-of-line testing.
followUpTargets: Ask how the candidate worked with factory test staff when new firmware reached production testers, and which end-of-line test failures they investigated.
